name: com.lazynext/ai-slop-checker
title: Lazynext AI Slop Checker
description: Detect AI slop in text, HTML, pages, and project folders. Free, no API key.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: List the full pattern corpus (categories + every rule with id, severity, kind, match, fix). Use this to know what the scanner flags.

tools.name: scan_text
tools.description: Scan plain text for AI-slop writing tells. Returns score (0-100), verdict, per-category breakdown, and every match with a fix suggestion.

tools.name: scan_html
tools.description: Scan HTML markup for AI-slop writing AND visual design tells (gradients, kickers, glassmorphism, stat rows, ...).

tools.name: scan_project
tools.description: Scan a local directory tree (prose/markup/styles/code lenses) and return a pooled report: score, top offending files, category breakdown. Local filesystem access only.

topFiles.description: how many top files to report (default 10)

tools.name: scan_render
tools.description: Run the rendered-tier design checks (r-*): kicker size, gradient text, tracked caps, glued arrows, marquee, hidden reveal, fold budget, screen word budget, section rhythm, fake progress, and WCAG contrast — all pure functions over a computed snapshot ({elements:[...]}, see src/render-checks.js). Pass an object snapshot; no browser needed.

snapshot.description: computed snapshot: { viewport?, documentStyle?, elements: [...], screens? }

url.description: http(s) URL to collect then check (requires the optional playwright collector)

tools.name: rewrite_text
tools.description: Apply conservative safe rewrites (whole-word synonym swaps and phrase deletions only) to a text. Returns the rewritten text plus the change list.

tools.name: judge
tools.description: Run the judgement checklist (--judge) over text, HTML, or a directory: the 5-question review (purpose/audience/decision/variety/defaults) with machine-flagged signals per question, a craft-floor gate (contrast/alignment/text-hierarchy/spacing/no-fake-data/no-decorative-effects) mapped from scanner evidence with human-checkbox items for the non-machineable parts, refusal scaffolds, and a machine-computed PASS | REVIEW | REFUSE verdict computed ONLY from machine-verifiable parts. Same input always gives the same verdict.

dir.description: directory path to judge — local filesystem access only
